# zhsein

> Uses inverse iteration to find right and/or left eigenvectors of a complex upper Hessenberg matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zhsein from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zhsein';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zhsein(
    order,
    side, eigsrc, initv,
    SELECT, strideSELECT,
    N,
    H, LDH,
    w, strideW,
    VL, LDVL,
    VR, LDVR,
    mm,
    M,
    WORK,
    RWORK,
    IFAILL, strideIFAILL,
    IFAILR, strideIFAILR
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `side` | `"left" \| "right" \| "both"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'both'`, `'left'`, `'right'`. |
| `eigsrc` | `"qr" \| "no-source"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'no-source'`, `'qr'`. |
| `initv` | `"no-init" \| "user"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'no-init'`, `'user'`. |
| `SELECT` | `Uint8Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideSELECT` | `integer` | Stride length for `SELECT` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `H` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDH` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `H`<br>Requires `LDH ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `w` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |
| `VL` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × mm</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDVL` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `VL`<br>Rejects `ldvl < 1 \|\| ((side === 'left' \|\| side === 'both') && ldvl < N)` |
| `VR` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × mm</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDVR` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `VR`<br>Rejects `ldvr < 1 \|\| ((side === 'right' \|\| side === 'both') && ldvr < N)` |
| `mm` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of columns in the arrays VL and/or VR. |
| `M` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Input/output (length-1 array): number of rows |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ N * N</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| `IFAILL` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length mm</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideIFAILL` | `integer` | Stride length for `IFAILL` |
| `IFAILR` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length mm</sub> | **out** · Output array |
| ↳ `strideIFAILR` | `integer` | Stride length for `IFAILR` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `side`:

  -   `= 'R'`: compute right eigenvectors only;
  -   `= 'L'`: compute left eigenvectors only;
  -   `= 'B'`: compute both right and left eigenvectors.
- `eigsrc`: Specifies the source of eigenvalues supplied in W:

  -   `= 'Q'`: the eigenvalues were found using ZHSEQR; thus, if H has zero subdiagonal elements, and so is block-triangular, then the j-th eigenvalue can be assumed to be an eigenvalue of the block containing the j-th row/column.  This property allows ZHSEIN to perform inverse iteration on just one diagonal block.
  -   `= 'N'`: no assumptions are made on the correspondence between eigenvalues and diagonal blocks.  In this case, ZHSEIN must always perform inverse iteration using the whole matrix H.
- `initv`:

  -   `= 'N'`: no initial vectors are supplied;
  -   `= 'U'`: user-supplied initial vectors are stored in the arrays `VL` and/or `VR`.
- `SELECT`: Specifies the eigenvectors to be computed. To select the eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue `W(j)`, `SELECT(j)` must be set to .TRUE..
- `N`: The order of the matrix H. $N \ge 0$.
- `H`: The upper Hessenberg matrix H. If a NaN is detected in H, the routine will return with `INFO=-6`.
- `w`: On entry, the eigenvalues of H. On exit, the real parts of W may have been altered since close eigenvalues are perturbed slightly in searching for independent eigenvectors.
- `VL`: On entry, if `INITV = 'U'` and `SIDE = 'L'` or 'B', `VL` must contain starting vectors for the inverse iteration for the left eigenvectors; the starting vector for each eigenvector must be in the same column in which the eigenvector will be stored. On exit, if `SIDE = 'L'` or 'B', the left eigenvectors specified by `SELECT` will be stored consecutively in the columns of `VL`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If `SIDE = 'R'`, `VL` is not referenced.
- `VR`: On entry, if `INITV = 'U'` and `SIDE = 'R'` or 'B', `VR` must contain starting vectors for the inverse iteration for the right eigenvectors; the starting vector for each eigenvector must be in the same column in which the eigenvector will be stored. On exit, if `SIDE = 'R'` or 'B', the right eigenvectors specified by `SELECT` will be stored consecutively in the columns of `VR`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If `SIDE = 'L'`, `VR` is not referenced.
- `mm`: The number of columns in the arrays `VL` and/or `VR`. $\mathrm{MM} \ge M$.
- `M`: The number of columns in the arrays `VL` and/or `VR` required to store the eigenvectors (= the number of .TRUE. elements in `SELECT`).
- `IFAILL`: If `SIDE = 'L'` or 'B', $\mathrm{IFAILL}(i) = j > 0$ if the left eigenvector in the i-th column of `VL` (corresponding to the eigenvalue w(j)) failed to converge; `IFAILL(i) = 0` if the eigenvector converged satisfactorily. If `SIDE = 'R'`, `IFAILL` is not referenced.
- `IFAILR`: If `SIDE = 'R'` or 'B', $\mathrm{IFAILR}(i) = j > 0$ if the right eigenvector in the i-th column of `VR` (corresponding to the eigenvalue w(j)) failed to converge; `IFAILR(i) = 0` if the eigenvector converged satisfactorily. If `SIDE = 'L'`, `IFAILR` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "both", "left", "right"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "no-source", "qr"
- `TypeError` fourth argument must be one of the following: "no-init", "user"
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` ninth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDVL < 1 \|\| ( ( side === "left" \|\| side === "both" ) && LDVL < N )`)
- `RangeError` thirteenth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDVL < 1 \|\| ( ( side === "left" \|\| side === "both" ) && LDVL < max( 1, mm ) )`)
- `RangeError` fifteenth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDVR < 1 \|\| ( ( side === "right" \|\| side === "both" ) && LDVR < N )`)
- `RangeError` fifteenth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDVR < 1 \|\| ( ( side === "right" \|\| side === "both" ) && LDVR < max( 1, mm ) )`)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zhsein.ndarray(
    side, eigsrc, initv,
    SELECT, strideSELECT, offsetSELECT,
    N,
    H, strideH1, strideH2, offsetH,
    w, strideW, offsetW,
    VL, strideVL1, strideVL2, offsetVL,
    VR, strideVR1, strideVR2, offsetVR,
    mm,
    M,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    RWORK, strideRWork, offsetRWork,
    IFAILL, strideIFAILL, offsetIFAILL,
    IFAILR, strideIFAILR, offsetIFAILR
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `side` | `"left" \| "right" \| "both"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'both'`, `'left'`, `'right'`. |
| `eigsrc` | `"qr" \| "no-source"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'no-source'`, `'qr'`. |
| `initv` | `"no-init" \| "user"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'no-init'`, `'user'`. |
| `SELECT` | `Uint8Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideSELECT` | `integer` | Stride length for `SELECT` |
| ↳ `offsetSELECT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `SELECT` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `H` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideH1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `H` |
| ↳ `strideH2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `H` |
| ↳ `offsetH` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `H` |
| `w` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideW` | `integer` | Stride length for `w` |
| ↳ `offsetW` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `w` |
| `VL` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × mm</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideVL1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `VL` |
| ↳ `strideVL2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `VL` |
| ↳ `offsetVL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `VL` |
| `VR` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × mm</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideVR1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `VR` |
| ↳ `strideVR2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `VR` |
| ↳ `offsetVR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `VR` |
| `mm` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of columns in the arrays VL and/or VR. |
| `M` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Input/output (length-1 array): number of rows |
| `WORK` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length ≥ N * N</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |
| `RWORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ N</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideRWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `RWORK` |
| ↳ `offsetRWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `RWORK` |
| `IFAILL` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length mm</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideIFAILL` | `integer` | Stride length for `IFAILL` |
| ↳ `offsetIFAILL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IFAILL` |
| `IFAILR` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length mm</sub> | **out** · Output array |
| ↳ `strideIFAILR` | `integer` | Stride length for `IFAILR` |
| ↳ `offsetIFAILR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IFAILR` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `side`:

  -   `= 'R'`: compute right eigenvectors only;
  -   `= 'L'`: compute left eigenvectors only;
  -   `= 'B'`: compute both right and left eigenvectors.
- `eigsrc`: Specifies the source of eigenvalues supplied in W:

  -   `= 'Q'`: the eigenvalues were found using ZHSEQR; thus, if H has zero subdiagonal elements, and so is block-triangular, then the j-th eigenvalue can be assumed to be an eigenvalue of the block containing the j-th row/column.  This property allows ZHSEIN to perform inverse iteration on just one diagonal block.
  -   `= 'N'`: no assumptions are made on the correspondence between eigenvalues and diagonal blocks.  In this case, ZHSEIN must always perform inverse iteration using the whole matrix H.
- `initv`:

  -   `= 'N'`: no initial vectors are supplied;
  -   `= 'U'`: user-supplied initial vectors are stored in the arrays `VL` and/or `VR`.
- `SELECT`: Specifies the eigenvectors to be computed. To select the eigenvector corresponding to the eigenvalue `W(j)`, `SELECT(j)` must be set to .TRUE..
- `N`: The order of the matrix H. $N \ge 0$.
- `H`: The upper Hessenberg matrix H. If a NaN is detected in H, the routine will return with `INFO=-6`.
- `w`: On entry, the eigenvalues of H. On exit, the real parts of W may have been altered since close eigenvalues are perturbed slightly in searching for independent eigenvectors.
- `VL`: On entry, if `INITV = 'U'` and `SIDE = 'L'` or 'B', `VL` must contain starting vectors for the inverse iteration for the left eigenvectors; the starting vector for each eigenvector must be in the same column in which the eigenvector will be stored. On exit, if `SIDE = 'L'` or 'B', the left eigenvectors specified by `SELECT` will be stored consecutively in the columns of `VL`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If `SIDE = 'R'`, `VL` is not referenced.
- `VR`: On entry, if `INITV = 'U'` and `SIDE = 'R'` or 'B', `VR` must contain starting vectors for the inverse iteration for the right eigenvectors; the starting vector for each eigenvector must be in the same column in which the eigenvector will be stored. On exit, if `SIDE = 'R'` or 'B', the right eigenvectors specified by `SELECT` will be stored consecutively in the columns of `VR`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If `SIDE = 'L'`, `VR` is not referenced.
- `mm`: The number of columns in the arrays `VL` and/or `VR`. $\mathrm{MM} \ge M$.
- `M`: The number of columns in the arrays `VL` and/or `VR` required to store the eigenvectors (= the number of .TRUE. elements in `SELECT`).
- `IFAILL`: If `SIDE = 'L'` or 'B', $\mathrm{IFAILL}(i) = j > 0$ if the left eigenvector in the i-th column of `VL` (corresponding to the eigenvalue w(j)) failed to converge; `IFAILL(i) = 0` if the eigenvector converged satisfactorily. If `SIDE = 'R'`, `IFAILL` is not referenced.
- `IFAILR`: If `SIDE = 'R'` or 'B', $\mathrm{IFAILR}(i) = j > 0$ if the right eigenvector in the i-th column of `VR` (corresponding to the eigenvalue w(j)) failed to converge; `IFAILR(i) = 0` if the eigenvector converged satisfactorily. If `SIDE = 'L'`, `IFAILR` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "both", "left", "right"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-source", "qr"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "no-init", "user"
- `RangeError` seventh argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, i is the number of eigenvectors which failed to converge; see `IFAILL` and `IFAILR` for further details.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zhsein()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZHSEIN`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zhsein.f).
-   `w` supplies the eigenvalues (e.g. from `zhseqr`) whose eigenvectors are wanted.
    `SELECT[j]` chooses which eigenvectors to compute; `M` returns how many.
-   `H` must be upper Hessenberg. Eigenvectors are found by inverse iteration and
    `IFAILL`/`IFAILR` flag any that failed to converge.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import Uint8Array from '@stdlib/array/uint8/lib/index.js';
import zhsein from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zhsein';

// Upper-triangular complex Hessenberg H (2-by-2, column-major) with eigenvalues 1 and 2:
const N = 2;
const H = new Complex128Array([ 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.5, 0.0, 2.0, 0.0 ]);

// Known eigenvalues (the diagonal of H):
const w = new Complex128Array([ 1.0, 0.0, 2.0, 0.0 ]);

// Compute the right eigenvector for every eigenvalue:
const SELECT = new Uint8Array([ 1, 1 ]);
const VL = new Complex128Array( N * N );
const VR = new Complex128Array( N * N );
const WORK = new Complex128Array( N * N );
const RWORK = new Float64Array( N );
const IFAILL = new Int32Array( N );
const IFAILR = new Int32Array( N );

// On exit, `m[ 0 ]` holds the number of computed eigenvectors:
const m = new Int32Array( 1 );

const out = zhsein( 'column-major', 'right', 'no-source', 'no-init', SELECT, 1, N, H, N, w, 1, VL, N, VR, N, N, m, WORK, RWORK, IFAILL, 1, IFAILR, 1 );

console.log( 'info: %d, m: %d', out, m[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZHSEIN`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZHSEIN uses inverse iteration to find specified right and/or left eigenvectors of a complex upper Hessenberg matrix H.

The right eigenvector x and the left eigenvector y of the matrix H corresponding to an eigenvalue w are defined by:

$$
H \, x = w \, x, y^h \, H = w \, y^h
$$

where $y^h$ denotes the conjugate transpose of the vector y.

### Further Details

Each eigenvector is normalized so that the element of largest magnitude has magnitude 1; here the magnitude of a complex number (x,y) is taken to be \|x\|+\|y\|.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
